backlog.spec: Replace construct_packing with: start from the existing two-ring layout, then run scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) over variables [x,y,r] (78 vars) maximizing sum r, with vectorized inequality constraints: r_i<=x_i, r_i<=1-x_i, same for y, and (xi-xj)^2+(yi-yj)^2-(ri+rj)^2>=0 for all pairs. Bounds r>=0. maxiter 500. At end shrink radii by 1e-12 and recompute via safe LP-based radii fix. Return centers, radii.
backlog.title: SLSQP joint optimize centers+radii

backlog.spec: Seeded numpy RandomState(0). Loop for ~200s wall time: sample 26 random centers uniformly in [0.05,0.95], radii init 0.05, run SLSQP joint optimization (x,y,r) with analytic-free vectorized constraints, keep best valid sum. Check time.time() to stop before 200s. Final shrink radii by 1e-12.
backlog.title: Multi-start SLSQP random inits

backlog.spec: Provide explicit constraint Jacobians (sparse-structured but dense array, pair index arrays from np.triu_indices) and objective gradient to SLSQP so each iteration is fast; this enables many more multistarts within 4 minutes. Use as the core solver for the other multi-start schemes.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: After any center optimization, fix centers and solve the LP maximize sum r s.t. r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distances, r>=0 with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Alternate: LP for radii, then SLSQP small-step moves of centers, repeat several times to polish.
backlog.title: LP radii refinement given centers

backlog.spec: Initialize centers on a perturbed hexagonal-ish lattice with rows of 5,5,6,5,5 (=26) or 6,5,5,5,5 variations, with jitter sigma 0.02 from seeded RNG, then run SLSQP joint optimization. Try several row patterns and keep the best.
backlog.title: Hex-grid based initialization

backlog.spec: Initialize 25 circles on a 5x5 grid with spacing 0.2 and one extra circle inserted at a random interstice, add jitter, then SLSQP joint optimization over multiple jitter seeds; keep best.
backlog.title: Square-grid 5x5 plus one init

backlog.spec: Stage 1: minimize -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2 + wall violation^2) with L-BFGS-B over (x,y,r), mu increasing 10,100,1e3,1e4 schedule. Stage 2: polish with SLSQP. Run from many random seeds.
backlog.title: Penalty-method gradient descent then SLSQP

backlog.spec: Starting from best SLSQP solution, perform perturbation loops: move 1–3 random circles (or the smallest circle) to random positions, reoptimize with SLSQP (limited maxiter 100), accept if sum improves (or by Metropolis with T=0.002). Run until 200s.
backlog.title: Basin hopping on centers

backlog.spec: After a solution, identify the smallest circles, remove one and reinsert at the location of the largest empty hole (point maximizing min distance to circle boundaries/walls via grid sampling), then reoptimize. Iterate and keep improvements.
backlog.title: Swap small circle relocation

backlog.spec: Initialize radii from a distribution: 4 corners large (0.12), center large, others small, with centers placed accordingly (corners, edge midpoints, interior), then SLSQP. Use random variations of the size assignment.
backlog.title: Radius-size-diverse init

backlog.spec: Fix four circles tangent to the corners initially (center at (r,r) etc.) with r~0.1 and remaining 22 random, then SLSQP with all free. Multi-start with seeds.
backlog.title: Corner-pinned structure

backlog.spec: Impose mirror symmetry about the diagonal x=y: 26 circles = k pairs plus m on-diagonal circles (e.g. 4 on diagonal, 11 pairs). Optimize reduced variables with SLSQP, then release symmetry and polish with full SLSQP.
backlog.title: Symmetry-constrained search

backlog.spec: Use 180° rotational symmetry: 13 free circles plus mirrored copies about (0.5,0.5). Optimize with SLSQP on 13 circles, then unconstrained polish. Many random starts.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetry init

backlog.spec: Simulated physics: circles with growing radii, repulsion forces resolved by iterative relaxation; radii grow by factor until jam, with random shaking, 2000 steps vectorized numpy. Then SLSQP polish from the jammed state.
backlog.title: Annealed radius-growth physics

backlog.spec: Run a few Lloyd iterations on random points in the square (grid-sampled Voronoi, 100x100 samples) to get evenly spread centers, then set radii by LP and polish via SLSQP. Multi-start.
backlog.title: Lloyd/Voronoi centering init

backlog.spec: Use scipy trust-constr with NonlinearConstraint on pair distances and bounds, from a good SLSQP solution, to attempt a tighter polish; compare and keep best valid.
backlog.title: Trust-constr alternative

backlog.spec: In SLSQP, only include pair constraints for pairs with center distance < 0.45 at the current iterate, re-select every outer iteration (repeat 5-10 outer rounds). Reduces constraint count from 325 to ~100 and speeds up so more restarts fit.
backlog.title: Active-set neighbor pruning

backlog.spec: At the end, identify active constraints (gap <1e-9), solve Newton on the KKT-like system, or simply iterate LP on linearized constraints (sequential LP with trust region 0.01 shrinking) to converge to machine precision, then subtract 1e-13 from radii and verify validity with strict check, shrinking further if any violation.
backlog.title: Exact tangency final polish

backlog.spec: Implement SLP: linearize pair constraints around current (x,y,r), solve with linprog highs for dx,dy,dr within trust region delta (start 0.05, halve on failure, grow on success), accept if true feasibility restored via LP radius repair. Run from many starts.
backlog.title: Sequential LP with trust region

backlog.spec: Enumerate row-count patterns summing to 26 (e.g., 5,5,6,5,5; 6,5,4,5,6; 4,5,5,5,4,3 ...) place circles evenly along rows with staggered offsets, SLSQP polish, pick best across patterns.
backlog.title: Rows 6-5-5-5-5 variants with different row counts

backlog.spec: Wrap whole pipeline in a while loop using time.time() with 210s budget and seeded RNG; each iteration random init + short SLSQP (maxiter 150) screening, and only top 5 screened results get full SLSQP (maxiter 1000) polish.
backlog.title: Randomized restarts with time budget loop

backlog.spec: Optimize with SLSQP allowing 1e-10 tolerance violations then final safe-fix: compute for each pair scale radii so r_i+r_j <= d_ij*(1-1e-12) and wall constraints using min, guaranteeing validity under zero tolerance.
backlog.title: Soft constraints then hard shrink

backlog.spec: Start from best solution and perturb: add Gaussian noise sigma 0.02 to all centers, reoptimize; repeat with sigma sweep {0.005,0.01,0.03,0.05}; keep best (iterated local search).
backlog.title: Weighted radii perturbation exploration

backlog.spec: Parametrize layout by ring counts (e.g., center 1, ring of 6, ring of 12, outer 7) with radii and ring offsets; use scipy differential_evolution with LP radii as fitness, then SLSQP full polish.
backlog.title: Differential evolution on a low-dim parametrization

backlog.spec: Use scipy dual_annealing with 52 center variables, fitness = -LP-optimal radii sum (linprog highs), limited maxfun, then SLSQP polish of the best.
backlog.title: Dual annealing on centers with LP fitness

backlog.spec: Optimize 27 circles then drop smallest, or optimize 25 circles plus add one in the largest hole, then reoptimize 26 with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Remove-one-circle from 27 packing

backlog.spec: Maximize sum r + t*sum log(slack) over all constraints using L-BFGS-B / Newton with t decreasing 1e-2 to 1e-7, from a feasible start (LP radii for random centers). Finish with SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior point

backlog.spec: Initialize with a few big circles (r≈0.14) at 4 corners and center, then fill remaining 21 by greedy placement: repeatedly place a circle at the point maximizing the max feasible radius (grid sampling 80x80), then SLSQP polish jointly.
backlog.title: Power-diagram aware init

backlog.spec: Greedy insertion: iteratively add circles at best grid hole, with random choice among top 5 holes (seeded), 26 total, then joint SLSQP. Repeat many randomized builds in time budget.
backlog.title: Greedy hole-filling plus ring structures

backlog.spec: At return, recompute radii as min over wall distances and 0.5*(d_ij - slack) scaling via LP, subtract 1e-12, assert strict double-precision checks (r<=x, x+r<=1, d>=ri+rj) and iteratively shrink by 1e-12 until all pass; return float arrays and python-sum equal np.sum(radii).
backlog.title: Final validity guard

backlog.spec: After spending ~50% of the time budget on multistart, take the best solution and run a basin-hopping loop until ~230s total: perturb all centers with Gaussian noise (sigma randomly chosen from 0.01, 0.03, 0.06), set radii to 0.8 of current, re-run SLSQP (maxiter 200) using the existing cons/jac, and accept if the sum improves (or with small Metropolis probability at temperature 0.002). Keep the global best and finalize it.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from best with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Generate starts by first running SLSQP for 27 circles (adapt n via parameter, build the helper functions for n=27) from random/staggered starts, then delete each of the circles with the smallest radii in turn to produce 26-circle starts with radii kept, and run SLSQP on 26. Use the best result. Make solve code parametric in n so both sizes reuse it.
backlog.title: Remove-one from 27-circle solution

backlog.spec: Reduce the problem: impose symmetry about the diagonal x=y (13 circle pairs, or some circles on the diagonal, e.g. 4 on-diagonal plus 11 pairs). Optimise only the free variables with SLSQP, then use the result as a start for the full unconstrained SLSQP polish. Try several on-diagonal counts (0,2,4,6 with matching pair counts) across restarts.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search space

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a cheap vectorized gradient-descent/Adam warmup on penalty energy: maximize sum r minus mu*(sum of squared overlap violations + wall violations), with mu annealed from 1 to 1000 over 500 steps from random starts. Feed the result into SLSQP. Run many more starts as the warmup is cheap, and screen them by warmup score before SLSQP on the top 20%.
backlog.title: Penalty growth physics warmup

backlog.spec: Initialise with explicit size heterogeneity: place 4 large circles (r~0.13) near the corners, 8 medium circles (r~0.11) along edges, and the rest small in the interior with jittered positions on a hex grid. Use these radii as r0 for SLSQP rather than a uniform 0.05-0.08. Randomise the counts (corner 4, edge 6-10) across restarts.
backlog.title: Size-diverse structured initialization

backlog.spec: Per start, run a first SLSQP stage with only pairwise constraints for pairs whose center distance is less than 0.4 (recomputed once), which makes the Jacobian much smaller and faster. Then re-solve with the full constraint set for the final polish. The speedup allows roughly 3x more starts within the budget.
backlog.title: Neighbor-pruned fast SLSQP

backlog.spec: Take the best solution and apply structured moves: pick a random circle, remove it, and re-insert it at the largest empty hole (found by sampling 2000 random points and maximizing distance to the nearest circle edge or wall), shrinking its radius to fit. Then run SLSQP. Repeat in a loop over the top 3 solutions, keeping improvements. Also try swapping two neighboring circles of very different radii.
backlog.title: Contact-graph perturbation moves

backlog.spec: For each start, first solve SLSQP with objective sum(w_i r_i) where w_i are random in [0.7,1.3], maxiter 100, then re-solve with w=1 from that solution. This diversifies the size distribution and escapes local optima where identical weights lock the structure.
backlog.title: Randomized radius-weight objective homotopy

backlog.spec: Build starts from a hexagonal lattice of spacing ~0.19 with random rotation angle and offset, keep the 26 points inside the square closest to the center (or add or drop random points to reach 26 exactly), jitter by 0.01, set r0=0.07 and run SLSQP. Use this for 40% of starts with random lattice angle in [0,30deg].
backlog.title: Hex-lattice with defects initialization

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best 3 results, re-run SLSQP with ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 1000 from them. Then compute the exact feasible radii by solving the LP in radii at fixed centers (linprog highs, with constraints r_i+r_j <= d_ij*(1-1e-13), r_i <= wall distance) and subtract only 1e-12 instead of 2e-9. Verify validity with the zero-tolerance check before returning; fall back to the former finalize if it fails.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish with minimal margin

backlog.spec: After multistart, take the best packing. Pick two circles with different radii that are neighbors or near neighbors (center distance < 0.3) and swap their centers. Set all radii to 0.8*their old values (min 0.02) and re-solve with SLSQP. Keep the result if it is better. Loop until the time budget ends. This explores permutations of sizes over the same site layout, which local SLSQP cannot do.
backlog.title: Contact-graph swap moves

backlog.spec: For half of the starts, enforce a diagonal-reflection symmetry. Generate 13 free circles (or 10 free plus 3 on the diagonal, which gives 23 total, then add 3 more free ones) and mirror x<->y to form the full set of 26 as 2k off-diagonal circles plus 26-2k diagonal circles. Use k=11 with 4 diagonal circles and k=12 with 2 diagonal. Run SLSQP on the full 26 circles from this symmetric init without enforcing symmetry afterwards, so it can break symmetry. Compare the results with random starts.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search space

backlog.spec: For each start, first run SLSQP with objective -sum(w_i r_i), where w_i = 1+0.5*u_i and u_i is uniform in [-1,1] (maxiter 100). This biases some circles to be larger. Then rerun SLSQP with the true objective from that solution. Use it for every third start. The perturbed objective moves the starts into different basins.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective homotopy

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, relax the random init with a vectorized soft-penalty method. Minimize -sum(r) + mu*sum(overlap^2 + wall violation^2) over (x,y,r) with L-BFGS-B, and ramp mu through 10, 100, 1000 and 10000. Then polish with SLSQP (maxiter 300). Use this for every other start in place of the raw random init.
backlog.title: Penalty gradient descent warmup

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP on 27 circles (generalize n via a function parameter) for about 25% of the budget. For each of several good 27-circle solutions, delete each of the 27 circles in turn, which gives 26-circle seeds. Run a short SLSQP on each, seeding from the shrunken radii. Keep the best valid result. Compare it with the existing multistart and use the better one.
backlog.title: Remove-one from 27-circle packing

backlog.spec: Seed starts with a mix of sizes: 4 corner circles of radius about 0.13, 4 edge-midpoint circles of radius about 0.11, 1-3 large interior circles of radius about 0.14, and the remaining circles of radius about 0.07 at jittered hex positions in the gaps. Jitter positions by 0.02. Use this for 30% of the starts, then run the usual SLSQP.
backlog.title: Size-diverse structured init

backlog.spec: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing over the 52 center coordinates in [0.03, 0.97]. The fitness is minus the optimal radii sum from scipy linprog (highs) with the centers fixed. The LP constraints are r_i+r_j<=d_ij and r_i<=wall distance. Use maxiter about 200 and a fixed seed, with the time budget capped at 40% of the total. Polish the best result with SLSQP, then continue multistart with the remaining time.
backlog.title: Dual annealing on centers with LP fitness

backlog.spec: For 40% of the starts, generate 13 random centers and radii and mirror them through (0.5,0.5), i.e. c -> 1-c. Then run the usual joint SLSQP without enforcing symmetry. Optionally use 12 pairs plus 2 circles at the center, offset slightly. Many near-optimal packings have approximate 2-fold symmetry, so this can shrink the search space.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetric init

backlog.spec: Change the finalize margin from 2e-9 to 1e-12. After the SLSQP polish, compute the exact radii by LP at the best centers (linprog highs, tight tolerances). Then subtract only 1e-13 per radius and check validity in float64 with a zero-tolerance test, and shrink a pair only if it fails. This recovers about 5e-8 of the sum. Pair it with a longer total budget of 230 seconds.
backlog.title: Finish with a high-precision margin

backlog.spec: After the multistart phase (about 50% of budget), run basin hopping from the incumbent best (c, r). Each step: copy best centers, perturb 2-4 randomly chosen circles by Gaussian noise sigma 0.05 (or all circles with sigma 0.01), set r0 = 0.9*r, then run the existing SLSQP (maxiter 200). Accept if the sum improves, or with Metropolis probability at temperature 0.002. Always keep the global best. Use finalize() before comparing. Replaces the remove-and-replace loop.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from best with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, pick two circles i, j with notably different radii (ratio >1.3) that are near each other, swap their centers, set radii to the swapped ones scaled by 0.9, and re-run SLSQP from there. This explores permutations of size assignment in the same topology. Accept only if the finalized sum improves. Loop until the time budget, with seed 0.
backlog.title: Contact-graph swap of two neighbouring circles of different size

backlog.spec: For half of the multistarts, optimize a symmetric packing: 13 free circles in the left half-plane x<=0.5 mirrored across x=0.5 (or, for variants, 1 on the axis plus 12 mirrored pairs, giving 25, plus 1 more on the axis). Build the z vector with fewer variables, expand to the full 26 via a linear map inside cons/jac (chain rule with the constant matrix), solve with SLSQP, then use the result as a seed for a full unconstrained SLSQP polish. Symmetry cuts the search space and may find high-quality structured optima.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search space

backlog.spec: Every 3rd multistart: draw 13 random centers in the square, add their reflections through (0.5,0.5) to get 26, assign matching radii 0.05-0.09 to each pair, jitter by 0.005, then run the normal full SLSQP (no symmetry enforced). Occasionally the polished result stays symmetric and reaches good basins.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetric init

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP, run a first SLSQP stage from each start maximizing sum(r) - 0.5*lam*sum((r-rbar)^2) pulling radii toward equality (lam=2, with analytic gradient), maxiter 100, then a second stage with the true objective from that result. Equalized radii give a hex-like jammed start, and the second stage lets sizes diversify.
backlog.title: Dual-phase objective homotopy to squared radii

backlog.spec: For random starts, first minimize -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0,overlap)^2 + wall violations^2) with L-BFGS-B using vectorized analytic gradients, with mu going 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4 and warm starts between stages (200 iterations each). Then run SLSQP from the result with maxiter 200. Use it on 1/3 of starts, with a different penalty form from earlier Adam attempts (exact gradients, deterministic quasi-Newton).
backlog.title: Soft penalty then hard shrink with L-BFGS

backlog.spec: Spend 15% of budget solving n=27 by SLSQP multistarts (generalise n through a parameter), then for the best few 27-solutions try removing each circle in turn (27 options), re-solve n=26 from the remaining centers/radii with SLSQP, and keep the best. Feed the result as the incumbent for the later refinement loop. Requires making solve routines parametric in n.
backlog.title: Remove-one from 27-circle packing

backlog.spec: Parametrize the seed as row counts from a pattern list plus continuous row y-offsets, per-row x-shifts and per-row radius scale (about 15 parameters). Run scipy differential_evolution (seed 0, popsize 10, maxiter 15) with fitness = -sum of radii after a short 60-iteration SLSQP from the built seed. Take the top 3 results, polish fully with SLSQP, and use as incumbents for the remaining time.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over low-dim row parametrization

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 2e-9 radius margin in finalize. Apply 1e-15-scale shrinkage: after SLSQP, run a 2-iteration Newton-like polish solving the active constraints exactly, then shrink each radius by only 1e-12 relative and verify in double precision, the same pair test as the checker (d - ri - rj >= 0 and walls), looping to increase shrink by 10x until valid. This recovers about 5e-8 of sum and guarantees validity.
backlog.title: Final high-precision margin tightening

backlog.spec: Add a symmetric multistart phase using about 25% of the time budget. Parametrize 13 free circles in the half-square x<=0.5, with circles near x=0.5 allowed on the axis. Mirror them to build 26 circles (axis circles are not duplicated, so use e.g. 11 mirrored pairs plus 4 on-axis, or 12 pairs plus 2 on-axis). Run SLSQP on the reduced variables with the same vectorized constraints built from the expanded set, or simply seed full SLSQP from the symmetric init and let it break symmetry. Keep the best result in the same best/best_val structure as the full search.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric reduced search

backlog.spec: For 30% of random starts, generate 13 random centers and radii and add their reflections through (0.5,0.5), giving 26 circles. Then run the normal full SLSQP from there (symmetry may break). Centrally symmetric packings are common in good packings for even n. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetric seeds

backlog.spec: During the multistart phase, keep a pool of the 8 best distinct solutions (distinct by sum of radii differing by more than 1e-6). In the final 30% of the time, pick a pool member at random and perturb it. Choose one of three moves at random: Gaussian jitter of all centers with sigma 0.02, swap of two neighbouring circles with different radii, or shifting a random 5-circle cluster by 0.05. Re-solve with SLSQP (maxiter 300) and insert the result into the pool if it improves on or enters the pool. This is iterated local search with a diversified pool, not only the single best.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-reoptimize ILS from top-K pool

backlog.spec: Add a phase where the 4 corner circles are tangent to two walls (x=r, y=r etc.), so each has one free variable, r. Use 22 free circles with SLSQP. Seed the other 22 from a random or staggered row layout of the interior. Pinned corners reduce degrees of freedom and often match the known best structure. Finish with a full free SLSQP polish from the result.
backlog.title: Corner-pinned reduced variables

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best solution and polish it with scipy trust-constr using the analytic Jacobian and a Hessian approximation of BFGS or SR1, with gtol 1e-12 and maxiter 500. Accept only if finalize() succeeds and the sum is larger. Also try polishing the top 3 distinct solutions from the multistart this way, since SLSQP may stop short of exact KKT points.
backlog.title: Trust-constr / augmented-Lagrangian polish

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, take a random start and run L-BFGS-B on a smooth penalized energy: -sum r + mu * (sum of squared pair overlaps + squared wall violations) with mu raised in the sequence 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4 and with radii as variables. Then switch to SLSQP. Apply this to 50% of the random starts, with a fully vectorized analytic gradient. This gives different basins than direct SLSQP from raw random starts.
backlog.title: Soft-min objective homotopy

backlog.spec: Seed starts with a prescribed size profile. Draw radii from a bimodal distribution: 4 large (0.12-0.14) circles, 12 medium (0.09-0.11), and 10 small (0.05-0.08). Place them by sequential random dart-throwing with rejection, largest first, shrinking radii by 0.9 on failure. Pass these as the SLSQP initial z0 for 30% of starts. This differs from the plain uniform radii used so far.
backlog.title: Radius-distribution prior init

backlog.spec: For half of the random starts, sample 14 to 16 of the centers on a band near the square boundary (distance from the wall uniform in [0.04,0.12]) and the remaining centers in the interior [0.2,0.8]. Best packings have many circles touching walls. Use initial radii of 0.07 for boundary points and 0.1 for interior ones, then run SLSQP as before.
backlog.title: Edge-biased center sampling

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, count tangent pairs and wall contacts (gap < 1e-7). Discard a solution early if fewer than 2n-ish contacts exist (for example below 55 total), as it is probably not a rigid local optimum. For those, run a second SLSQP from the result with a tiny random jitter (sigma 1e-3) of the centers and keep the better one. This spends effort only on promising basins and fixes premature SLSQP stops.
backlog.title: Active-contact-count restart filter

backlog.spec: Replace the plain objective by a homotopy: first solve with objective -sum(r^p) with p=0.5, which pushes toward equal radii, then p=1.0, then p=1.5 (rewards size diversity), each as SLSQP with maxiter 100 warm-started from the previous stage, and a final p=1 solve. Use it on a random 40% of starts with the analytic gradient p*r^(p-1). Different p values change basin selection and may reach the variable-radius structures that plain p=1 misses.
backlog.title: Parallel-tempering style radius-sum cap

backlog.spec: Add a symmetric solver variant: 13 free circles with centers (x,y) and their images (1-x,1-y) with equal radii (optimise 13 centers and 13 radii; build the full 26 for constraints, with the Jacobian obtained by the chain rule or by mapping z_full = T @ z_red where T is a constant matrix). Run SLSQP multistart in this reduced space for the first 25% of the time budget, then use the best symmetric result as the seed for the full unconstrained SLSQP (breaks symmetry) and continue with the existing phases. Keep the final result only if valid.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetric search

backlog.spec: For the first 20% of the time, solve with a left-right mirror symmetry about x=0.5: 10 mirrored pairs plus 6 circles on the axis (x fixed at 0.5), or 13 pairs and 0 axis circles; try both counts. Build the full vector via a constant linear map T from reduced variables and use J_full @ T. Take the best result as a start for the full SLSQP polish (with small noise), then the existing multistart continues.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric reduced search

backlog.spec: During the multistart keep a pool of the top 8 distinct packings (distinct by sorted radii differing by more than 1e-3). In the final phase, repeatedly pick a pool member at random, perturb 3-6 circles randomly (swap two circles of different radii, or relocate a circle to the biggest hole), re-solve with SLSQP maxiter 200, and insert it into the pool if it is better than the worst and distinct. Return the pool's best.
backlog.title: Pool-based ILS with top-K diversity

backlog.spec: In the final phase, from the best packing pick two touching circles with different radii (gap<1e-7, radius ratio >1.2) and swap their centers. Set the radii to the average of the two plus 0.5*the old radii, shrink all by 3%, and re-solve with SLSQP. Also try swapping non-adjacent pairs of circles whose radii differ. Accept on improvement. Run this as 50% of the post-multistart time.
backlog.title: Radius-swap moves on contact graph

backlog.spec: For random starts, first minimise -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + wall violations^2) using scipy L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients, mu going 10, 100, 1000, 1e4 with 100 iterations per stage, starting from tiny radii of 0.02. Pass the result to SLSQP (maxiter 300). Apply to 1/3 of the starts and discard any whose penalty result has sum r less than 2.4.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty L-BFGS then hard SLSQP

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 distinct packings from the multistart. Spend the last 10% of time polishing each with scipy trust-constr (method 'trust-constr', analytic Jacobian via NonlinearConstraint with the existing cons/jac, Hessian BFGS/SR1, gtol 1e-12, maxiter 500), with the constraint written as the non-squared form d - r_i - r_j >= 0. Then run finalize and keep the best valid one.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: Run 6x more starts, each with SLSQP maxiter 40 and ftol 1e-6; keep a pool of the best 12 by the sum of radii after clipping (via finalize or LP); then fully converge those 12 with maxiter 400 and ftol 1e-12. Use a different RNG seed (e.g. 12345). Budget: 50% screening, 25% polishing, 25% remaining for the drop-and-replace phase.
backlog.title: Large-count-of-starts with short SLSQP screening

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP multistart solve, run a stage with the objective -sum(r^p) for p=0.5 (equalising radii), 100 iterations. Then run -sum(r^p) with p=0.8, then p=1 (final). Analytic gradient p*r^(p-1) with r clipped to at least 1e-3. Apply it to 1/3 of the starts and compare the results with random starts.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius homotopy

backlog.spec: Seed starts with a prescribed radius distribution: sample the radii from a bimodal mix (4 corners r~0.13, 8 edge circles r~0.11, 14 interior of r~0.08 with noise) and centers by Poisson-disk dart throwing with minimum distance r_i+r_j (retry until the 26 are placed, shrinking radii by 5% on failure). Use this on 1/3 of the starts, with SLSQP using the radii as the initial values.
backlog.title: Size-hierarchy prescription seeds

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best centers c. Run scipy dual_annealing (seeded) over the 52 center coordinates within bounds of c±0.04, with the fitness -sum(LP-optimal radii) from scipy linprog (highs) on the pair constraints r_i+r_j<=d_ij and wall constraints, with maxiter limited to about 15% of the time budget. Then polish with SLSQP from the result and return if better.
backlog.title: Dual annealing over center jitter with LP radii

backlog.spec: Change rng = np.random.default_rng(0) to a different fixed seed (e.g. 12345) in solve_packing so the multistart explores different basins. Keep everything else unchanged. The result is repeatable, and the seed alone can shift the best basin found.
backlog.title: Different RNG seed sweep

backlog.spec: For every third multistart, build the initial centers as 13 random points p_i plus their reflections (1-p_i) through the square centre. Use similar radii for each pair. Run the usual full 78-variable SLSQP from this seed without enforcing symmetry, so it can break symmetry if that helps. Symmetric starts reduce the search space and hit good basins more often.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetric multistart

backlog.spec: On every fourth multistart, seed with 13 points mirrored about x=0.5, where some points may lie on the axis. Use 26 total: k on-axis points plus (26-k)/2 mirrored pairs, with k in {0,2,4}. Then run the unconstrained SLSQP polish from the seed.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric multistart seeds

backlog.spec: Run each multistart with maxiter=80 and ftol=1e-8 to screen cheaply, and keep the top 6 distinct results by sum of radii. After the screening budget (50% of time), polish each of the top 6 with maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-12. Use the remaining time on the existing drop-and-replace phase from the best polished result.
backlog.title: Shorter SLSQP with more starts, then full polish of the top few

backlog.spec: After the search, run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr', using the analytic jac and a NonlinearConstraint with lower bound 0 on the cons function. Use the existing jac, and a BFGS or SR1 Hessian update. Start from the best z with maxiter 300. Accept the result only if finalize() succeeds and the sum is higher.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the best

backlog.spec: Before the hard SLSQP, solve a penalty stage with L-BFGS-B. Minimise -sum r + mu*sum(max(0, violation)^2) over the same variables, with mu going 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4. Use this as the warm start for SLSQP on every other random start. Use vectorised numpy gradients.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius homotopy

backlog.spec: In the final phase, besides removing small circles, remove 2 circles at once. Pick them at random among circles with fewer than 3 contacts, or at random from the whole set with 30% probability. Reinsert each at the largest empty hole found by dense sampling of 5000 points, then run SLSQP. Accept only improvements.
backlog.title: Contact-graph removal and reinsertion of the largest-neighbour circle

backlog.spec: Sample initial radii from a bimodal prior: 4 corner circles at about 0.13, 8 edge circles at about 0.11 and the rest about 0.09. Place centers by Poisson-disk-style rejection sampling with minimum distance equal to the sum of the two radii times 0.8. Use this on every third start with full SLSQP.
backlog.title: Radius-prior init

backlog.spec: In the first SLSQP stage for random starts (maxiter 100), add a small term 1e-3 * sum((x-0.5)^2+(y-0.5)^2) to the objective. Provide the gradient, so circles spread out toward the walls. Then re-run SLSQP on the pure objective from that result. This is a regularised continuation that avoids bad jammed states.
backlog.title: Hybrid objective regularizer: add small centre-spread term

backlog.spec: In the final phase, with probability 0.3 per iteration apply a collective move to the best packing instead of removing a circle. Either rotate a random half of the circles about the centre by a small angle of 0.05 rad, or shift one random row/column band of circles by 0.03 along its axis. Clip to the square, shrink the radii by 0.9, and re-solve with SLSQP. Accept only improvements.
backlog.title: Perturbation with larger-scale shear/rotation moves

backlog.spec: Change the multistart in solve_packing: run each SLSQP start with maxiter=80 and ftol=1e-8 for the first 60% of the budget, keeping every result's (centers, radii) in a list. Then take the top 12 by sum of radii (after finalize-free raw sum) and re-run full SLSQP (maxiter=500, ftol=1e-12) from each. Then run the existing drop-and-replace phase from the best. This gives roughly 3-4x more starts than now.
backlog.title: Time-split seed portfolio with polish of top-K

backlog.spec: For half of the starts, optimise only 13 circles (x,y,r) and enforce the other 13 as the images (1-x,1-y,r) through the centre. Build the full 26-circle arrays inside cons/jac via a linear map matrix M (78 x 39) so that z_full = M @ w. Jacobian is J_full @ M. Solve with SLSQP from random starts, then use the result as the seed for an unconstrained 26-circle SLSQP polish. Keep the best overall.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetric reduced SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the existing search, take the best packing and run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' using the same cons as NonlinearConstraint (lower bound 0, upper bound inf) with the analytic jac, gtol=1e-12, maxiter 2000, within about 20 seconds. Keep the result only if finalize() accepts it and its sum is larger.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: In some starts, add a regularizer to the SLSQP objective: obj = -sum(r) + lam*sum(r**2), with lam sequence 0.5, 0.2, 0.05, 0 across four SLSQP stages of 80 iterations each, warm-started. The quadratic term pushes towards equal radii, so it reaches different basins than plain sum-of-radii. Apply it to 40% of random starts with the gradient g = -1 + 2*lam*r.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap homotopy

backlog.spec: In the post-search phase, replace the drop-and-replace move with a collective move on the best packing. Choose a random disc in the square, centre c and radius 0.25. Rotate all circles inside it about c by a random angle in ±0.4 rad, or shear them by 0.05. Shrink the radii by 0.8 and re-solve with SLSQP. Accept if the sum improves. Alternate with the existing move 50/50.
backlog.title: Contact-graph shear/rotation moves

backlog.spec: In the final phase, pick a random 6-circle cluster (one centre plus its 5 nearest neighbours) from the best solution. Re-sample the cluster centres uniformly in their bounding region (expanded by 0.05), keep the other 20 circles fixed, and solve only the cluster variables with SLSQP (18 centres/radii vars) from 5 random draws. Then run a full 26-circle SLSQP polish on the best draw. Accept if improved. This is a cheap, local, large-move search.
backlog.title: Weighted-radius LP-guided large-neighbourhood search

backlog.spec: Seed starts from a random placement in a larger domain [0,L]^2 with L=1.3. Run 30 steps of simple gradient descent on a penalty for overlap (radii fixed 0.1), while the domain shrinks linearly from L to 1 and the positions are scaled by 1/L at each step. Then feed the result to SLSQP with initial radii 0.07. Use it on 1/3 of starts. This is a compression protocol, which is different from the earlier Lloyd and jam seeds because the packing is driven by the shrinking walls.
backlog.title: Annealed square-to-wall compression seeds

backlog.spec: Add constraints r[a] >= r[b] for a random partial order in the first SLSQP stage. Pick 6 random 'big' indices and 20 'small' ones, and require r_big >= r_small + 0.01 for 6 randomly paired (big, small) pairs. Solve for 100 iterations, then drop the extra constraints and run the full SLSQP. It forces a hierarchical radius layout without prescribing the radii values. Use on 1/3 of random starts.
backlog.title: Two-size-class constrained radius ordering

backlog.spec: Keep the 10 best distinct final solutions from the multistart (distinct if sorted radii differ by more than 1e-3). In the final phase, pick two, choose a random line through the square, and take circles on one side from parent A and the other side from parent B. If the count is not 26, remove the smallest extras or add circles at the largest holes (the sampled clearance method). Run SLSQP with radii x0.9 and keep any improvement in the pool.
backlog.title: Pool crossover of two good packings

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed pats list in the structured seeds with a generator. Sample k in {5,6,7} rows, then draw row counts that sum to 26 with each count between 3 and 7. Give each row a random x-offset in [-0.5/m, 0.5/m] and a y-position (i+0.5)/k plus a jitter of 0.03. Also randomly choose columns instead of rows. Use these for all odd iterations. It widens the structural diversity, which the nine fixed patterns do not cover.
backlog.title: Row-structure scan with variable row counts and random offsets

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 solutions from the multistart. After the search, for each one run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' using the same cons as NonlinearConstraint (lb=0, ub=inf) with the analytic jac, gtol=1e-12, xtol=1e-14, maxiter 500, from the SLSQP solution. Then pass the result through finalize and keep it if its sum is higher. This is bounded to about 20 seconds of the budget.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: In the post-search phase, pick a random circle among those with 5 or more contacts (gap<1e-7). Remove it together with its 2 nearest neighbours. Reinsert 3 circles at the top-3 clearance points from 4000 random samples in the freed region (the removed circles' bounding box expanded by 0.1), with radii 0.02. Jitter all centers by N(0,0.002) and run SLSQP with maxiter 200. Accept only if the sum improves. Time-box each trial.
backlog.title: Contact-graph removal and reinsertion

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP, in half the multistarts, run a short SLSQP stage on the objective -sum(r) + lam*sum(1/(r+0.01)), with lam=0.002 and maxiter 80. This penalizes tiny circles and spreads the radii. Then run the normal objective from the result. Gradients are analytic: d/dr = -1 - lam/(r+0.01)^2.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius homotopy

backlog.spec: On every 5th multistart, solve a reduced problem with 13 free circles (x,y,r). Their partners are at (1-x,1-y) with the same r, which gives 26 circles. Run SLSQP on the 39 variables with constraints built through the expansion map. Then use the full 78-variable solution as the seed for a full unconstrained SLSQP with maxiter 300. Seeds are random points.
backlog.title: Point-reflection symmetric reduced SLSQP seeds

backlog.spec: Run many starts with SLSQP maxiter=60 and ftol=1e-7, storing the raw z for each. Use 60% of the budget for this. Then fully polish (maxiter 400, ftol 1e-12) the top 15 by the screened sum, using the remaining time. Report the best finalized result. This gives about 5x more starts than now.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full-polish batching

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed pattern list with random generation. Choose k rows in 5..6, and draw row counts that sum to 26 with each count in 3..7. Random shift per row in [-0.5,0.5]/count, and random row y spacing jitter. Use this for the structured half of the starts, with N(0,0.02) jitter. Keep the SLSQP path unchanged.
backlog.title: Row-structure scan with random offsets

backlog.spec: In each SLSQP start, add bounds r<=cap, starting at cap=0.09 and relaxing in 3 stages (0.09, 0.12, 0.5) with maxiter 100 each, warm-starting from the previous stage. This avoids runaway big circles early and equalizes sizes. Apply it to every third start.
backlog.title: Radius-cap annealing schedule

backlog.spec: Replace the drop-and-replace post-phase with moves on a random disc of radius 0.2-0.35: rotate the centers in the disc by a random angle up to 30 degrees about the disc center, and swap two circles of different radii within it. Shrink all radii by 0.9, run SLSQP with maxiter 200 and accept only if improved. Mix 50/50 with the existing move.
backlog.title: Large-shear and rotation moves in the final phase

backlog.spec: For 25% of starts, set radii r0 by position. Use 0.11 for points within 0.12 of a corner, 0.09 along edges, and 0.07 in the interior. Sample 4 corner circles, 12 edge circles and 10 interior circles with jitter. Run SLSQP directly with maxiter 300. Keep the seed RNG deterministic.
backlog.title: Wall-band radius-ordered seed

backlog.spec: In the final phase, take the best packing and run SLSQP maximizing sum(w*r) with random weights w in [0.8,1.2], drawn per circle, with maxiter 150. Then reoptimize with w=1 from the result. Accept if the true sum improves. This explores neighbouring contact graphs through weighted objectives from the incumbent rather than from random starts.
backlog.title: Alternate-objective perturbation of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the 10 best distinct SLSQP solutions from the multistart (70% of budget). In the remaining time, build children by choosing a random line (random angle through a random point in [0.3,0.7]^2), taking circles from parent A on one side and parent B on the other, then fixing the count to 26 by removing the smallest circles or adding circles at the largest holes (sampled clearance). Radii are scaled by 0.95, then re-solved with the existing SLSQP. Insert the child into the pool if it is better than the worst member. Keep the final return as the best.
backlog.title: Pool crossover of two packings

backlog.spec: During the multistart, keep the top 5 finalized packings. After the multistart, polish each with scipy minimize method 'trust-constr' using the same cons, jac and bounds (Hessian as BFGS or SR1, xtol 1e-12, maxiter 500). Run finalize on the output and keep it only if the sum improves. Use the remaining time for the usual drop-and-replace phase on the best packing.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: Replace the multistart with a two-stage batch. Stage 1: run about 3x more starts, each with SLSQP maxiter 60 and ftol 1e-8. Record the objective, without finalize. Stage 2: take the top 15 by objective and re-run SLSQP with maxiter 400 and ftol 1e-12 from the stage 1 result. Finalize and keep the best. Spend 60% of the budget on this, then run the existing drop-and-replace phase.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish batching

backlog.spec: For a third of the random starts, run a first SLSQP stage with an added upper bound on every radius, r_i <= cap. Start with cap=0.09 and run stages with cap 0.09, 0.11, 0.13, 0.5, warm-starting each stage from the previous result (maxiter 80 each). This forces similar-sized circles first, then lets the large and small circles diverge. Finish with an uncapped full solve.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing. Pick two touching circles with a radius ratio above 1.3 and swap their centers. Set both radii to the mean times 0.9 and re-solve with SLSQP. Also try swapping two non-touching circles of different size. Accept only if improved. Loop until the time is up. Run this in place of the current drop-and-replace phase for the second half of the leftover time.
backlog.title: Pair-swap of neighbours with different radii

backlog.spec: Add a phase using a reduced SLSQP over 13 free circles, with 8 circles on the diagonal x=y (1 free coordinate) and the others in mirror pairs (x,y)/(y,x). Run this for 15% of the budget with random starts. Then expand to the full 26-circle problem and run a full unsymmetrized SLSQP from the result, with a tiny noise of 1e-3. This lets the polish break the symmetry. Keep the best over all runs.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric reduced search about the diagonal

backlog.spec: On a random 30% of starts, first run SLSQP maximizing sum(r) + lam*sum(r^2) with lam=2.0 for 100 iterations. This favors unequal radii. Then run with lam=0.5 for 100 iterations, and then with lam=0 until convergence. The gradient is 1+2*lam*r for each radius. Keep the final result only if finalize is valid.
backlog.title: Radius-spread regularizer homotopy

backlog.spec: In the final phase, remove two circles at once: one among the 4 smallest and one random with at least 4 contacts. Re-insert both at the two largest clearance holes found from 5000 samples, with a spacing constraint between the holes. Use radii of 0.03 for both, add noise of 0.005, and run SLSQP. Accept on improvement. This is a bigger move than the single-circle move.
backlog.title: Contact-graph defect relocation of a pair

backlog.spec: Run the multistart with a different RNG seed each time that is derived from the 'it' counter (seed = 1000+it), so the starts depend only on the index. Within the same 70% budget, the first 40% of iterations use random starts and the remaining ones use perturbations (sigma 0.04) of the best-so-far centers, with radii reset to 0.05, followed by SLSQP. This replaces the use of one global generator and gives a sequence of local searches in the best basin.
backlog.title: Lagrangian rescue: free multiple seeds with the fixed seed list

backlog.spec: Replace the single fixed rng seed 0 with a loop over seeds: split the multistart phase (70% of budget) into 4 equal sub-phases, each using a different fixed seed (0, 1, 2, 3) for its own default_rng, while keeping the global best across all sub-phases. Keep the later drop-and-replace phase unchanged. This diversifies the random starts and keeps the run reproducible.
backlog.title: Seed sweep with short runs, keep best seed

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the 10 best distinct packings found in multistart (distinct if the sum differs by more than 1e-5). In the post-multistart phase, repeatedly pick two pool members, take a random vertical or horizontal cut line at coordinate in [0.3,0.7], and combine the circles of A left of the cut with the circles of B right of it. If the count is not 26, remove the smallest circles or add circles at the largest holes found by random sampling. Run SLSQP (maxiter 300) from the result with radii scaled by 0.9. Accept if better than the incumbent and add it to the pool.
backlog.title: Pool crossover of two good packings

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct SLSQP results. After the search, polish each with scipy trust-constr (using the existing jac, and hessian as BFGS or SR1, with gtol 1e-12, maxiter 500, and NonlinearConstraint lb=0 ub=inf). Then run finalize and keep the best. Limit this to about 20 seconds in total.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the top candidates

backlog.spec: Run many more starts using SLSQP with maxiter 60 and ftol 1e-6, until 50% of the budget has passed. Keep the top 12 by the sum of radii. Then re-run SLSQP with maxiter 400 and ftol 1e-12 from each of them. Run the usual drop-and-replace phase from the best result. This is about 4x more starts for the same time, with full convergence only for the promising ones.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish batching

backlog.spec: For random starts, first run SLSQP with the objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-mean(r))^2) with lam=2 (analytic gradient), maxiter 100. Then run it again with lam=0.5, and finally with lam=0 until convergence. Warm-start each stage from the previous one. The regularizer favours equal-sized circles first, which is a different basin selection from plain starts. Use it on 30% of the starts.
backlog.title: Radius-spread regularizer homotopy

backlog.spec: Seed starts with a structure of 16 circles near the walls and 10 in the interior. Put the 16 on the boundary at equal spacing along the perimeter, with a 0.08 inset. Place the 10 interior circles on a jittered 3-4-3 staggered pattern inside [0.25,0.75]^2. Use initial radii 0.09 for border circles and 0.12 for interior ones. Use this for 25% of the starts with a random perimeter phase offset and jitter sigma 0.02. Then run the normal SLSQP.
backlog.title: Border-ring plus interior architecture

backlog.spec: Generate a hex lattice with spacing d drawn from [0.17,0.21], a random rotation and a random offset. Keep the points inside [0.04,0.96]^2. If more than 26 remain, drop the extra points with the lowest wall clearance. If fewer than 26 remain, add the largest holes. Use radii d/2 as the start. For this seed type, use a different lattice from earlier tries: alternate rows with random per-row shifts and with one row spacing compressed by 10%. Run SLSQP on 20% of the starts.
backlog.title: Hex lattice 26-of-N subset selection

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best packing and identify the active constraints: pairs with gap < 1e-7 and wall contacts. Solve the square system of active equalities for (x,y,r), using least squares Newton iterations (np.linalg.lstsq on the Jacobian of the active constraints) until the residual is under 1e-15. Then shrink the radii with a 1e-13 margin through finalize. Keep the result only if the sum of radii is higher. This removes the SLSQP tolerance slack, which is about 1e-9 and larger than the margin.
backlog.title: Active-set LP-Newton final refinement

backlog.spec: After the existing search finishes (reserve about 25 s), take the best (centers, radii) and run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same joint [x,y,r] problem. Use the analytic gradient and the constraint Jacobian as a sparse or dense matrix, and use NonlinearConstraint with lower bound 0 (upper bound inf) on cons. Take the result only if finalize() accepts it and the sum is larger than the current best. The aim is to reach a more exactly converged vertex than SLSQP did.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: Keep the 10 best distinct local optima from the multistart, with distinct meaning sums differing by more than 1e-4. In the post-search phase, pick two of them. Apply a random reflection or rotation by a multiple of 90 degrees to one. Choose a random line through the square. Take the circles on one side of the line from parent A and the circles on the other side from parent B. Fix the count to 26 by dropping the smallest extra circles, or by adding circles at the largest holes. Polish with SLSQP (radii scaled by 0.95) and keep the result if it improves.
backlog.title: Pool crossover of two good packings

backlog.spec: Spend 60% of the time on many cheap starts: SLSQP with maxiter=60 and ftol=1e-7, with no finalize call. Keep the 12 starts with the largest objective. Spend the remaining time re-running SLSQP with maxiter=400 and ftol=1e-12 from each of them, finishing with finalize(). Seed the RNG with 0. This tests the benefit of 5 to 10 times as many basins visited.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish batching

backlog.spec: After finding the best packing, identify the active constraints (pair gaps below 1e-7 and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT system for tangency with Newton iterations on those equalities. Use least squares on the [x,y,r] unknowns with a sum-of-radii Lagrangian, or use an LP step on the linearized active set. Iterate 5 times. Subtract a margin of 1e-12 and accept only if finalize() is valid and the sum is larger.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton refinement on the contact graph

backlog.spec: For one third of the starts, run SLSQP stages in sequence. In each stage, add the bound r_i <= cap, with cap taken from the sequence 0.10, 0.12, 0.15, 0.5. Use the previous stage's solution as the start, with 80 iterations per stage. Then do the full unconstrained solve. The cap forces more equal radii first, so later stages can break symmetry. This differs from a fixed 0.09 cap because the cap is annealed upward over four stages.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: In the post-search phase, choose a random disc of radius 0.2 in the square. Remove all circles whose centers lie in it, which is k circles. Re-seed k new centers in that disc using Poisson-disk sampling with random jitter. Set their radii to the mean radius of the removed circles. Run SLSQP on all circles with a 150-iteration cap. Accept if the sum improves. This is a localized large-neighbourhood move with a variable k, unlike the earlier 6-circle cluster resampling with a fixed count.
backlog.title: Cut-and-reflow Voronoi relaxation of removed region

backlog.spec: Add inequality constraints that fix a size ordering. Sort the circles of a start by random initial radius. For stage one, require r_(i) >= r_(i+1) for consecutive circles in the ordering, using a linear constraint. Solve with SLSQP. Then drop the ordering constraints and re-solve. The ordering breaks permutation symmetry and prevents duplicate basins. Half the starts use a random ordering and half use ordering by distance from the square center, with large circles in the middle.
backlog.title: Radius-order-constrained two-class model

backlog.spec: Replace rng.random starts with scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol (scrambled, seed 0) points, taking 52-dimensional blocks (26 centers) so that starts cover the space evenly. Hash each result by its sorted radii rounded to 3 decimals. Skip re-polishing duplicates. Use the saved time for more starts. Keep the structured seeds on the odd iterations.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Sobol multistart with deduplicated basins

backlog.spec: Add a parametrized generator. The row counts are from the pattern list. Each row has its own radius r_k and a random horizontal offset. Place the centers at row heights set so that adjacent rows are tangent (y spacing sqrt((r_a+r_b)^2 - dx^2)), then scale the whole thing to fit the unit square. Use this as the start for SLSQP with 30% of the starts. This is a geometric start, not a lattice with noise.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with variable per-row radius parameters

backlog.spec: For 30% of the starts, first maximize -sum(r) plus 0.5*sum((r - mean(r))^2 * -1), that is, reward variance in radii so that the solver tries bimodal packings. Use 120 SLSQP iterations. Then switch to the true objective, -sum(r), for the full solve. Use the analytic gradient, which for the variance term is 2*(r-mean). Starts with the best final sums are kept as usual.
backlog.title: Lagrangian-free squared-radius objective then switch

backlog.spec: During the first 70% multistart, keep a pool of the 10 best distinct SLSQP results (centers, radii). In the post phase, repeatedly pick two pool members, choose a random line (random angle and offset through the square), take centers of A on one side and centers of B on the other (optionally reflect/rotate B by one of the 8 square symmetries first), and if the count is not 26, drop the smallest-radii extras or add random points in the largest holes. Run SLSQP (maxiter 300) from that seed with radii 0.9x of the parent radii, and insert into the pool if better or distinct. Keep the best overall.
backlog.title: Pool crossover of two good packings

backlog.spec: Replace the multistart loop with two stages. Stage 1 (first 45% of budget): many starts with SLSQP maxiter 60, ftol 1e-8, recording (sum radii, z). Stage 2: sort by the sum of radii, take the top 15 and run full SLSQP maxiter 400, ftol 1e-12 on each from the stage-1 result. Keep the best, then finish with the existing drop-and-replace phase for the rest of the time. Seed RNG with 0.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish batching

backlog.spec: Replace the random uniform initial centers on the even starts with scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol (scrambled, seed 0) 52-dim points, taking each point as 26 centers scaled to [0.04,0.96]. Skip any start whose sorted radii vector after SLSQP is within 1e-4 (L-inf) of an already-seen result, to avoid wasting time on repeats, and print nothing. Keep the rest of the design.
backlog.title: Sobol multistart with basin dedupe

backlog.spec: Parametrize a packing as R rows (R in 5..7) with per-row count m_r (sum 26), per-row y position, per-row x offset and per-row nominal radius. Sample these randomly for a seed, build centers and radii from them, then run SLSQP from the seed. Draw counts from compositions of 26 with parts 3..7. Use for 40% of starts, with the radii initialised to the row radius rather than 0.05-0.08.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with per-row radius parameters

backlog.spec: For 30% of starts, run a first SLSQP stage (maxiter 120) minimizing -sum(r^2)/2 times a constant (gradient -r) to favour unequal radii, then a final stage with the linear objective from the stage-1 solution. Compare with the existing solver using the same constraint and Jacobian functions.
backlog.title: Squared-radius then linear objective switch

backlog.spec: In the post phase, remove two circles chosen at random among the 8 smallest, sample 4000 random points, compute clearance, and place two new circles at points from the top 15 clearances that are at least 0.1 apart. Seed radii 0.97x the old and 0.03 new, jitter 0.003, run SLSQP maxiter 300, and accept if better. This is a larger neighbourhood than the single drop-and-replace.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert-two LNS

backlog.spec: Before the main loop, spend 15% of the budget running 8 independent short multistarts, each with a different RNG seed (0..7) and about 1.5% of the budget. Pick the seed whose best was highest, then spend the remaining 70% continuing the multistart with that RNG seed's state restarted from a new default_rng(seed+100). Finish with the drop-and-replace phase.
backlog.title: Seed sweep with short runs

backlog.spec: Keep the 5 best distinct multistart results. At the end, for each, run scipy trust-constr with NonlinearConstraint using the existing cons and jac (lower bound 0, upper inf), objective -sum r with the analytic gradient and a Hessian of zeros (BFGS not required), gtol 1e-12, maxiter 500, in a 40-second total time cap. Finalize each and return the best valid one.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 8 structure. Replace the single rng seed 0 with a list of seeds [0,1,2,3]. Run each seed's multistart for 12% of the budget (total ~50% of the 70% phase) and keep a global best. Then run the drop-and-replace phase from the global best for the remaining time. This diversifies basins while keeping the seed-0 trajectory as the first segment.
backlog.title: Seed sweep on slot-8 design with time split

backlog.spec: Run many starts (random and row-pattern) with SLSQP maxiter 60 and ftol 1e-7 for 45% of the budget. Store every result with its sum. Take the top 12 by sum, and re-run each from its screened solution with maxiter 400 and ftol 1e-12. Pick the best after finalize. Use the remaining time for the slot 8 drop-and-replace phase.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish of top-K

backlog.spec: In the post phase, remove two circles that touch each other, or two of the smallest, from the best packing. Sample 4000 random points and take the two best-clearance points that are at least 0.1 apart, which gives two new circles. Initialize their radii at 0.03 and shrink the others by 0.97, then run SLSQP. Accept the result if it improves the best. Replace the current single-drop move with this one for half of the iterations.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert-two LNS

backlog.spec: Add a reduced multistart: choose a row count k in 5..7 and per-row circle counts summing to 26. Parametrize the row y-positions, a per-row x-offset and a per-row spacing. Draw these randomly with a seeded rng and build the seed centers with radii from the local spacing. Then run the full SLSQP. Use it on 30% of the starts, replacing the fixed pats list.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with per-row parameters

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT system for the active set with a few Newton iterations on x, y, r, using least squares and the multipliers from the LP dual. Check whether any multiplier is negative. If so, drop that contact and re-solve with SLSQP started from the point. Keep the result only if the finalized sum increases.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton refinement of contacts

backlog.spec: On 30% of multistarts, run SLSQP stages in which the objective stays the sum of r but each radius has an upper bound cap that decreases from 0.20 to 0.13 to 0.10 and finally is released to 0.5. Use 80 iterations per stage. The caps force many mid-size circles first, and the release lets the structure break symmetry. Use the final stage's solution as the result.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: For random starts, run a vectorized L-BFGS-B on the penalty objective -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + wall violations^2). Use mu going from 30 to 3e4 in 5 stages and analytic gradients. Then run SLSQP for the last polish with maxiter 200. Apply it on every second random start, with a different random radius initialization, 0.02 to 0.12.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty L-BFGS with a hard final SLSQP

backlog.spec: On 25% of the starts, seed 16 centers in a band of width 0.1 to 0.15 around the walls with initial radii 0.08 to 0.11 and 10 centers in the interior with initial radii 0.11 to 0.14 (larger interior). Run SLSQP with linear constraints enforcing r_interior >= r_wall only in a first 100-iteration stage, then drop the ordering constraints and re-run the full SLSQP.
backlog.title: Wall-band radius-ordered seed

backlog.spec: In the post phase, pick a random circle and take its 5 nearest neighbours. Rotate the cluster about its centroid by a random angle of 20 to 60 degrees and swap the radii of two random members. Clip centers into the square and set radii at 0.9 of the originals. Run SLSQP with maxiter 300, and accept if the sum improves. Use it on 50% of the post-phase iterations.
backlog.title: Contact-graph rotation of a cluster

backlog.spec: In solve_packing, replace the single rng seed 0 by a list of 4 seeds (e.g. 0,1,2,3). Split the multistart phase (70% of the budget) equally across seeds, each with its own default_rng(seed) and its own it counter, keeping the global best. Keep the final drop-and-replace phase unchanged on the global best. This diversifies basins while keeping reproducibility.
backlog.title: Seed sweep over several fixed seeds with split budget

backlog.spec: During the multistart phase, run SLSQP with maxiter 60 and ftol 1e-7 from many starts (the same seed mix as now). Keep a list of the 12 best (by finalized sum of radii) raw z vectors. At 60% of the budget, re-run SLSQP with maxiter 400 and ftol 1e-12 from each of these candidates and take the best. Then continue with the existing final phase. Use the remaining time budget accordingly.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish of top-K

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, identify active constraints (pair gaps < 1e-8, wall gaps < 1e-8). Solve the square or least-squares system of active equalities (dist_ij = r_i + r_j, wall distances = r) with a few Gauss-Newton or lstsq steps on [x,y,r] to reach exact tangency, accept only if the finalized sum increases. Then apply the existing shrink margin. Gain is limited to the final 1e-9 digits, but it is cheap.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton refinement of contact graph

backlog.spec: Replace the post-multistart phase move: remove two circles (one random among the 6 smallest, one random neighbour of it), choose the 2 largest holes from 4000 random points by greedy clearance (second hole after inserting the first), re-seed with radii 0.03, jitter 0.003, and run SLSQP. Accept if the sum improves. Seeded rng.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert-two LNS

backlog.spec: For one third of random starts, run SLSQP stages with added bound r_i <= cap, with cap = 0.11, 0.10, 0.12, 0.5 over four stages of 70 iterations each, then a final full SLSQP. This acts as a regularizer that equalizes radii early, then releases it.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: Add a seed family: choose 5 or 6 rows with counts from the patterns, but give each row its own y-position, x-offset and a radius estimate sampled from a uniform distribution (rows near the wall smaller). Place centres by these parameters, set the initial radii from the row radius, and run SLSQP. Use it on 25% of starts, drawn from a seeded rng.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with per-row parameters

backlog.spec: At the end of the multistart phase, take the top 3 packings and polish each with scipy trust-constr using the analytic Jacobians (constraints as NonlinearConstraint with bounds (0, inf)), gtol 1e-12, maxiter 500. Finalize each with the shrink and keep the best. Skip if less than 20 seconds remain.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: On 30% of starts, first run 100 SLSQP iterations minimizing -sum(r^2) (gradient -2r), which favors unequal sizes, then switch to the linear sum objective from the result. Implement via a flag in the obj and grad functions.
backlog.title: Squared-radius to linear objective switch

backlog.spec: In the final phase, with the best packing, run SLSQP with an objective of -sum(w_i r_i), where w_i = 1 + 0.3*uniform(-1,1), for 150 iterations from the incumbent plus 0.005 noise, then run the unweighted SLSQP to finish. Accept if the unweighted result improves. Seeded.
backlog.title: Perturbed-incumbent basin hopping with random weights

backlog.spec: For the last 30% of the budget, generate starts by keeping the incumbent's 18 largest circles (centres and radii*0.95) fixed as initial values, and resample the 8 smallest circles uniformly at random in the free space (rejection sample points with clearance greater than 0.02). Run SLSQP over all variables and accept if the sum improves. This gives a larger neighbourhood than single-circle replacement.
backlog.title: Biased hole-aware multistart from the incumbent shell

backlog.spec: Change solve_packing so the multistart phase is divided into 4 equal slices (each ~17% of the budget), each slice using a different fixed rng seed (0, 1, 2, 3) for its own default_rng, with the structured-pattern index also restarting per slice. Keep the global best across slices. Keep the slot-8 post-phase (drop and re-place small circles) for the last 30%. This diversifies basins while staying reproducible.
backlog.title: Seed sweep with split budget

backlog.spec: In the multistart phase run SLSQP with maxiter 60 and ftol 1e-7 on many starts, storing (sum, z) in a list. At 60% of the budget, take the top 8 distinct candidates (sums differing by more than 1e-4) and re-run SLSQP from each with maxiter 500, ftol 1e-12. Then run the slot-8 drop-and-replace phase from the best polished result.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish of top-K

backlog.spec: After the search, identify contacts of the best packing (pair gaps <1e-6, wall gaps <1e-6). Solve the square system of active equations (tangency and wall distances) for x, y, r by Newton with least squares (np.linalg.lstsq) for up to 20 iterations from the best z. Accept only if the resulting radii pass the finalize checks and have a larger sum. This gives exact tangency precision beyond SLSQP tolerance.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton refinement of contacts

backlog.spec: On a third of the random multistarts, first run SLSQP stages where the objective is sum(r) minus lambda*sum(r^2) with lambda annealed from 3 to 0 across four stages of 80 iterations (the gradient is -1+2*lambda*r), then finish with the plain linear objective. This discourages one huge circle early and lets the sizes spread, giving different basins.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: Add a parametric seed family: choose 5-6 rows with counts summing to 26, give each row its own radius parameter, and place the row y-positions cumulatively from the radii. Space circles in each row evenly with a half-spacing stagger between adjacent rows. Optimize the roughly 10 row parameters (radii, stagger) with scipy Nelder-Mead on a fast LP-radii fitness, 20 random restarts. Then use the top 5 results as SLSQP seeds before the regular multistart.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with per-row radii

backlog.spec: In the post-phase, remove the two circles with the lowest radius, which are not adjacent. Compute the two largest empty holes by grid sampling of 4000 points with clearance and farthest-point selection, so the second hole is at least 0.1 away from the first. Reinsert the circles there with radius 0.02 and run SLSQP at maxiter 300. Accept only if the sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert-two LNS using holes

backlog.spec: On every fourth start, sample 16 centers uniformly along a band of 0.08-0.15 inside the walls and 10 centers uniformly in the interior [0.25,0.75]^2. Initialize radii at 0.07 for the band circles and 0.12 for the interior circles. Use a min-distance rejection sampler of 0.08 between centers. Then solve with SLSQP as usual.
backlog.title: Wall-band radius-ordered seed

backlog.spec: Draw starts from a scrambled Sobol sequence (scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol, d=52, seed 0, with random_base2 blocks) for the odd, non-structured starts. Hash each finished solution by sorted radii rounded to 3 decimals, and skip the post-processing of duplicates. When 20 consecutive solves hit duplicates, switch the starts to a wider jitter (0.04) of the top-3 solutions to escape repeated basins.
backlog.title: Per-run random time-step seeds with basin dedupe

backlog.spec: For 60% of the budget run SLSQP with maxiter 60 and ftol 1e-6 from many starts (random and row patterns). Keep a list of the top 6 results by radius sum, deduplicated by sum within 1e-4. Then re-run SLSQP on each of them with maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-12 starting from the screened solution. Use the remaining time for drop-and-replace from the best.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish of top-K

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 distinct finished packings. Polish each with scipy trust-constr using the analytic cons and jac, with NonlinearConstraint lower bound 0 and upper bound inf, gtol 1e-12 and maxiter 300. Pass a sparse-friendly hessian via BFGS. Accept a result only if finalize() returns a valid packing with a larger sum.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: Build seeds from a parametrized row model. Pick 5 or 6 rows and per-row counts that sum to 26. Give each row its own base radius, drawn from rng uniform(0.06,0.13), with x-offsets drawn at random and rows stacked by cumulative 2*radius spacing and normalized into the unit square. Use these as SLSQP initial centers and radii for 30% of starts. Replace the fixed pats list for those starts.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with per-row radius parameters

backlog.spec: Before the main SLSQP on 25% of random starts, run four short SLSQP stages with an upper bound on every radius that is tightened from 0.16 to 0.14, 0.12 and 0.10, then removed. Reuse the previous solution as the start of each stage. This pushes the optimizer through different size distributions than the uncapped solve.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, identify the active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-8). If the count of active constraints is at least 3n, solve the square system of tangency equations with scipy.optimize.least_squares (method lm, xtol 1e-15). Use it to remove the residual slack. Subtract 1e-12 as the margin, run finalize, and keep the result only if the sum is larger.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton refinement of contacts

backlog.spec: For 30% of random starts, minimize -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + wall violations^2) with L-BFGS-B on the vector [x,y,r], with analytic gradients. Increase mu through 10, 100, 1000 and 1e4. Then run SLSQP from the result with a normal maxiter. This is a different basin selection from a pure SLSQP start.
backlog.title: Soft penalty L-BFGS then hard SLSQP

backlog.spec: Spend 20% of the time solving n=25 with the existing SLSQP multistart. Add a 26th circle at the largest hole and optimize. Separately, solve n=26 normally. Take the best of the two. Parametrize solve_packing by n, and apply a hole-filling insertion with radius 0.02 followed by SLSQP with 300 iterations on 20 perturbed variants of the 25 packing, each using noise sigma 0.01.
backlog.title: Bold: 27 to 25 circle ladder

backlog.spec: Replace the single rng seed 0 with a list of 4 seeds (0, 1, 2, 3). Give each seed 15% of the 0.7*time_budget multistart phase (shared best), running the existing multistart loop per seed with rng=default_rng(seed). Keep the slot 8 drop-and-replace phase on the overall best. This tests whether other seeds hit a better basin at the same total cost.
backlog.title: Seed sweep with split budget

backlog.spec: After the search, identify the active constraints of the best packing (gap < 1e-8). Solve the square system of active constraints plus stationarity by Newton iterations (or least squares with np.linalg.lstsq) to get machine-precision tangency. Accept the result only if finalize validates it and the sum improves. Fall back to the original otherwise.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton KKT refinement

backlog.spec: Make solve_packing parametric in n. Solve n=25 for 15% of the budget, add one circle in the biggest hole (shrinking radii by 3%), and re-solve with n=26 for another 15%. Use the result as an extra incumbent for the drop-and-replace phase. Also seed the multistart phase with these n=25 solutions plus one random circle.
backlog.title: 27 to 25 circle ladder

backlog.spec: On a third of random starts, run SLSQP stages with a cap on every radius that anneals from 0.12 down to 0.5 (effectively off) in 4 steps of 80 iterations each, via modified bounds on r. Finish with the normal full SLSQP. This tests whether limiting the early big circles changes the basins reached.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: On random starts, run an L-BFGS-B augmented-Lagrangian stage: minimize -sum(r) + (mu/2)*sum(max(0, -c_i + lam_i/mu)^2) for 6 outer iterations, updating lam, with mu from 10 to 1e4. Pass the result to the SLSQP polish. Use the analytic gradient built from vectorized constraints.
backlog.title: Pair-constraint augmented Lagrangian soft start

backlog.spec: Parametrize seeds as rows with counts from the existing patterns, per-row y positions, per-row horizontal offsets and per-row stretch drawn at random (sigma 0.05). Add Gaussian jitter of 0.01 and run SLSQP. Use this for 40% of the iterations in place of the fixed staggered rows, and keep all other iterations unchanged.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with per-row parameters

backlog.spec: Use 50% of the budget for starts that run SLSQP with maxiter 60 and ftol 1e-6, keeping the 8 best raw results by sum. Then re-run SLSQP on each of them with maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-12. Finish with the drop-and-replace phase on the overall best. Use seed 0 and keep the 70% structure.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish of top-K

backlog.spec: In the post-multistart phase, remove two circles (one from the 4 smallest, one random neighbour within 0.25) and reinsert both at the two largest distinct clear holes found by 5000 random probes, with a minimum separation between the reinserted points of 0.1. Re-solve with SLSQP (maxiter 300), accept only if the sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert-two LNS using holes

backlog.spec: On 30% of random starts, add a term lambda*sum((r-mean(r))^2) to the SLSQP objective, with its analytic gradient. Run it with lambda 0.5 for 100 iterations, then 0.1 for 100, then drop it and run the original full solve. A positive lambda favors uniform radii at first; this tests whether that leads to different basins.
backlog.title: Radius-spread regularizer homotopy

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 8 structure (multistart then drop-and-replace). Change the RNG seed from 0 to 1 and run a full job; previously only seeds 0, 12345 and the 4-way split were tried. Choose a seed by hand from {1,2,3,7,42}; use 7 for this slot. Keep everything else identical so the result is repeatable and comparable.
backlog.title: Seed sweep on slot-8 design, split budget

backlog.spec: In each SLSQP call, include only pair constraints for pairs whose initial center distance is below 0.45, then after the solve verify all pairs in finalize (it already shrinks radii on overlap). Re-solve once with the full constraint set warm-started from the result only for the top candidates (sum within 0.01 of best). This should give about 2x more starts per second. Do not use outer rounds that drop constraints permanently (slot 12 broke).
backlog.title: Constraint-count-aware SLSQP with active neighbor list

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP on random starts, run 30 outer iterations of an augmented Lagrangian method over (x, y, r). Minimise -sum r plus the multiplier terms for the overlap and wall constraints, using L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients, and update the multipliers each round. Then hand the result to SLSQP. This is different from the plain quadratic penalty tried in slot 36 because the multipliers give a near-feasible, well-conditioned start.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty augmented Lagrangian start

backlog.spec: Spend 60% of the budget running SLSQP with maxiter 60 on many starts. Keep the 5 best by raw sum of radii (relaxed). Re-run full SLSQP (maxiter 500, ftol 1e-12) from each. Then spend the remaining time on the slot 8 drop-and-replace phase starting from the best. Use polish iterations that continue from the screened z, not from the finalized one.
backlog.title: Short-screen then full polish of the top 5

backlog.spec: In the post phase, remove the two smallest circles or two random circles. Compute the largest empty holes on a 200x200 grid by the distance to the nearest circle surface or wall, taking local maxima as hole centers. Reinsert two circles in the top holes, with radius 0.5 times the hole clearance. Run SLSQP and accept only if the sum improves. Use 50% of iterations for this move and 50% for the existing move.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert-two using hole detection
