backlog.spec: After the search, identify active constraints (gap below 1e-8) of the best packing. Solve the KKT system for the squared-distance constraints using least-squares Newton (numpy lstsq) on the variables with multipliers from the SLSQP result. Take steps until the residual is below 1e-14. Then shrink radii by 1e-12 and verify validity. Fall back to the unpolished packing if validity fails or the sum drops.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton KKT refinement

backlog.spec: Solve n=27 for 20% of the budget with the multistart. Then for each pair of touching circles (up to 30 pairs), merge them into one circle at the weighted center with radius the sum of the radii times 0.6. Run SLSQP with the 26 circles. Keep the best. This differs from slots 21 and 27 (deletion) because it merges rather than removes.
backlog.title: Two-phase 27-to-26 with large circle merge

backlog.spec: In the post-multistart drop-and-replace phase, raise the SLSQP maxiter to 600 and set ftol to 1e-14. Reduce the noise on the re-placed circle to 0.001, and try candidate radii 0.02 and 0.05. The goal is to finish convergence in basins where 300 iterations ended early. Compare the sum before and after to judge if any basins were unfinished.
backlog.title: Lower SLSQP ftol with more iterations in the post phase

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 8 structure (multistart SLSQP, then drop-and-replace). Make solve_packing run K=3 independent phases. Each phase gets its own RNG, seeded with 0, 1 and 2, and runs for about 1/3 of the 0.7*budget multistart time. Keep the global best across phases. The final drop-and-replace phase then starts from the global best. The point is to hedge against a bad seed. Seed 0 alone already gives -2.6360, so keep seed 0 first.
backlog.title: Seed sweep on slot-8 design, split budget

backlog.spec: Build seeds from a row model. Draw 5 or 6 rows. Each row gets a count (the counts sum to 26), a y position, an x offset and a radius drawn from N(0.1, 0.02). Place the circles evenly along each row, then add Gaussian jitter of 0.01. Initialise SLSQP radii from the per-row radii. Use this on 40% of starts.
backlog.title: Hex-row architecture with per-row radius parameters

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best packing and identify the active contacts (gap < 1e-6). Solve the KKT system of the contact-constrained max-sum-radii problem with a Newton or least-squares step, taking the multipliers from an lstsq fit. Iterate up to 20 steps. Keep the result only if the pairwise and wall checks pass after the 1e-12 shrink.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton KKT refinement

backlog.spec: For screening starts, use only pair constraints for pairs whose center distance is under 0.4. After solving, re-check all pairs. If any are violated, re-solve with the full constraint set from that point. This gives 2-3x more starts in the multistart budget. Keep the full SLSQP for the final result.
backlog.title: Pair-constraint pruned fast SLSQP screening

backlog.spec: For 50% of the budget, run short SLSQP starts (maxiter 80). Keep the 12 best by radius sum, requiring each to differ from the others by a sorted-radii L2 distance above 0.01. Then run the full SLSQP (maxiter 500, ftol 1e-12) on each. Use the leftover time for the drop-and-replace phase on the best.
backlog.title: Basin-diverse pool then polish

backlog.spec: Alternate two steps. First, solve the LP for the optimal radii at fixed centers (scipy linprog, highs). Then take a gradient step on the centers, using the LP dual variables as the contact forces. After 50 iterations, switch to SLSQP. Apply this to the best 3 multistart results to look for basins that SLSQP alone misses.
backlog.title: Radius-ordered LP-alternating optimization

backlog.spec: On 30% of random starts, run an SLSQP stage that maximizes sum(r^2) for 100 iterations. This favors uneven radii. Then switch to the linear sum objective for the full SLSQP. Use the stage-1 result as the start. Compare against the pure linear baseline.
backlog.title: Squared-radius to linear objective switch

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 8 structure (multistart then drop-and-replace). Make solve_packing take a seed. Before the main run, spend 20% of the budget running 8 candidate seeds (1..8) for 2.5% of the budget each using only the multistart phase, record best value per seed. Then spend the remaining time continuing with the best seed, with its RNG re-created and iterated deterministically from its start, so the full multistart plus post-phase proceeds as in slot 8. Return the best packing seen overall.
backlog.title: Seed sweep on slot-8 design with per-seed short trial

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing. Loop: fix the radii, solve an LP over center displacements (linearized non-overlap constraints, trust region 0.01, maximizing nothing but slack t on all constraints) to open up gaps, then re-solve full SLSQP from the result. Accept if the sum of radii improves. This pushes the packing along flat directions in the contact graph that SLSQP stalls on. Use the remaining 25% of the time.
backlog.title: Alternating LP radii / SLSQP centers with contact-driven moves

backlog.spec: For every third multistart, before SLSQP run 5 outer iterations of an augmented Lagrangian method on the overlap constraints (inequality multipliers updated per pair and wall, L-BFGS-B inner solves with analytic gradients, 150 iterations each), maximizing sum of radii. Feed the result to SLSQP with maxiter 300. It's different from the quadratic penalty because the multipliers give accurate active sets.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian soft start

backlog.spec: Seed SLSQP from a design with 4 corner circles radius 0.12 tangent to the walls, 8 edge circles radius 0.10 along the walls between corners at random positions, and 14 interior circles on a jittered hex lattice with radius 0.09. Randomize the counts: edge circles 6..10, interior the rest to total 26. Use this seed on 30% of starts, with noise 0.01 on the centers. Run SLSQP with maxiter 300.
backlog.title: Three-size-class seeded architecture with 4 big corners removed

backlog.spec: In the post-phase, instead of random drop-and-replace, compute the Delaunay triangulation of the incumbent centers plus 4 mirrored boundary points, find the triangle circumcenters with the largest inscribed hole radius, remove the circle with the smallest radius, and insert the new circle at the top-3 holes in turn with initial radius equal to the hole radius. Run SLSQP from each candidate and accept improvements. Deterministic hole ranking rather than 3000 random sample points.
backlog.title: Delaunay-based hole insertion with a full re-solve at lower n

backlog.spec: In the post-phase, keep the incumbent and a current state. Each step perturbs the current state (drop-and-replace of a small circle plus noise 0.005), re-solves with SLSQP, and accepts a worse result with probability exp((new-cur)/T) where T decays linearly from 0.003 to 0.0002 over the phase. Track the global best and return it. This differs from greedy acceptance, which has always been stuck at -2.6360.
backlog.title: Replica pool with simulated-annealing acceptance

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing, identify circles with no contacts (rattlers, gap > 1e-4 with all neighbours and walls), and remove them from the optimization. Re-solve the remaining circles with SLSQP using ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 1000, then re-grow the rattlers to the maximum radius via closed-form clearance. The speed-up lets the post-phase run more iterations on the smaller problem.
backlog.title: Larger SLSQP precision: reduced variable set via fixing contacts

backlog.spec: Use a different objective for the first SLSQP stage: maximize sum(r) minus 0.05 times the variance of the Voronoi cell areas (approximated by nearest-neighbour distance squared) so that the layout starts evenly spread. Then switch to the pure sum objective. Apply it to 25% of random starts and compare their results with the baseline starts. Use numerical gradients only for the regularizer term via an analytic form on the nearest-neighbour distance.
backlog.title: Voronoi-power-weighted radii objective with lifted center variance

backlog.spec: Seeds from lattices: choose from square, hex and rhombic lattices with random angle in [0, 90), a random spacing giving between 26 and 40 points inside the unit square, a random offset, and drop random extras to reach 26. Radii initial equals 0.4 times the nearest-neighbour spacing. Apply on 30% of starts. Run SLSQP as usual. Differs from earlier hex-lattice seeds by including rhombic and square lattices with random shear.
backlog.title: Batch with random rotation of the square in the seed lattice

backlog.spec: Solve a 13-circle packing problem with the same SLSQP code (parametric n) to maximize the sum of radii, repeated for 10% of the budget. Then double: replace each circle of radius r at (x,y) with two circles of radius 0.5r displaced by random orientation ±0.5r from the center, then SLSQP the 26-circle problem. Use the top 10 coarse solutions. Gives a hierarchical basin structure not tried before.
backlog.title: Two-phase halving: coarse 13-circle pair model then split

backlog.spec: Before the main search, for each of 8 fixed seeds (0..7) run the slot-8 multistart loop for 6 seconds with its own default_rng(seed) and record the best sum. Pick the best 2 seeds and give each 40% of the remaining time budget, restarting its RNG from the seed. Keep the slot-8 drop-and-replace phase for the last 30% on the overall best. Keep the finalize function unchanged.
backlog.title: Seed sweep with short trials

backlog.spec: Add a seed generator with 5-6 rows. Row counts are drawn from the existing pats list. Each row has a vertical position and a horizontal offset as free parameters. Optimize these parameters with scipy Nelder-Mead for about 150 evaluations per seed. Fitness is the LP-optimal sum of radii at the resulting centers (linprog with variables r, constraints r_i+r_j<=d_ij and wall limits). Feed the best 5 parameterizations into SLSQP as starts, using 15% of the budget.
backlog.title: Hex-row seeds with per-row radii via Nelder-Mead

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 distinct solutions from the multistart in a pool. In the last 10% of the time, polish each with scipy trust-constr using the analytic Jacobian and a tight gtol. Also use SLSQP restarts with ftol 1e-15. Take the best valid result after finalize.
backlog.title: Trust-constr augmented polish of the top 3 solutions

backlog.spec: After the multistart, run a Metropolis walk over local optima. The move is drop-and-replace of 1-2 small circles followed by SLSQP. Accept a worse result with probability exp(-delta/T), with T going from 0.003 down to 0.0002. Keep the global best separately and return it. This walk can escape the incumbent basin, where greedy acceptance cannot.
backlog.title: Basin-diverse pool with simulated-annealing acceptance

backlog.spec: On 25% of starts, seed the centers from a 26-point subset of a square or hex lattice of random spacing 0.17-0.2. Rotate it by a random angle and shift it randomly. Take the 26 points that are most interior to [0.04,0.96]^2. Add noise sigma 0.01 and set the radii to 0.05. Then run the normal SLSQP.
backlog.title: Rotated-square lattice seeds

backlog.spec: First solve a 13-circle packing with SLSQP at a larger scale. Replace each circle with two circles. The two circles lie along a random direction, are separated by 0.5 of the parent radius, and each has 0.6 of the parent radius. Run SLSQP on the resulting 26 circles as a start. Do this for 15% of the time budget with many random 13-circle solutions.
backlog.title: Coarse 13-pair model then split

backlog.spec: After the search, identify the active contacts of the best packing (gap<1e-7). Solve the KKT system for the stationary point with those contacts as equalities, using numpy lstsq in a Newton iteration with multipliers. Accept the result only if it passes the validity check with a 1e-12 margin and has a larger sum. Use the smaller margin to gain 1e-8.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton KKT refinement

backlog.spec: Inside each multistart, solve SLSQP with only pair constraints whose initial center distance is under 0.4. Check all pairs after the solve. If any are violated, add them and re-solve once from the result. This makes each solve about 2x faster and allows about 2x more starts in the same budget. Retain the seed 0 RNG.
backlog.title: Larger batches of SLSQP with active-pair pruning

backlog.spec: In the final phase, replace the drop-and-replace move. Solve SLSQP from the incumbent with the objective sum(w_i r_i), where w_i is drawn uniformly from [0.5,1.5] for 80 iterations. Then re-solve with the true objective sum(r). Accept the result if it improves on the incumbent. This changes the contact graph through moves that are not purely geometric.
backlog.title: Weighted-objective perturbation basin hopping

backlog.spec: Replace the single multistart (seed 0, 70% budget) with 6 sequential windows of ~11% of the budget each, with RNG seeds 0..5 recreated at each window start. Run the multistart within each window, and keep a global best. Then give the final 30% to drop-and-replace from the global best. Slot 95 used 4 seeds at 12%; here use more, shorter windows and also skip any start whose first 60-iteration SLSQP objective is below the window best by more than 0.05.
backlog.title: Time-sliced seed portfolio with per-seed best retention

backlog.spec: For every random start, before the main SLSQP, run a 60-iteration SLSQP on a modified objective -sum(r) + lam*sum over pairs of exp(-d_ij/0.08) with lam=0.002 using the same constraints, then drop the term and run the usual SLSQP. This spreads centers uniformly and avoids clumped starts. Apply to 50% of random starts.
backlog.title: Linear-in-time radius-sum penalty on center spread (soft repulsion prior)

backlog.spec: Make solve_packing parametric in n. Spend 15% of the budget solving n=24 (multistart SLSQP). For each of the top 5 distinct solutions, find the 2 largest holes by dense grid sampling (clearance to circles and walls), insert 2 circles of radius 0.03 there with small noise, and run SLSQP for n=26. Keep the best valid result as the incumbent for the post-phase.
backlog.title: Variable-n warm start: 26 = 24 solved + 2 inserted at holes

backlog.spec: In the final polish of the best packing only: run SLSQP using only pair constraints with center distance < r_i+r_j+0.15, then check all pairs for violation. If any violations exist, add those pairs and re-solve, repeat up to 4 times. Use this with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-15 on the top 3 pool solutions. This gives a different precision path than the full-constraint solve.
backlog.title: Constraint-generation SLSQP with active-set refresh

backlog.spec: On 30% of random starts, generate centers by dart-throwing Poisson-disk sampling with minimum distance proportional to a random radius field: radius larger in the middle (0.11) and smaller at edges (0.07) by a random linear blend, followed by 3 Lloyd steps. Use these radii as r0 and run the usual SLSQP.
backlog.title: Voronoi-based random start from jittered Poisson-disk with size gradient

backlog.spec: Run starts in generations: each generation creates 12 starts, runs each for 50 iterations of SLSQP with ftol 1e-7, then continues only the top 3 to maxiter 300 with ftol 1e-11. Keep the global best across generations. This is a successive-halving schedule over generations rather than one global screening pass.
backlog.title: Batch of 4 random SLSQP starts in lockstep with early culling

backlog.spec: In the post phase, with probability 0.5 per iteration take the incumbent centers, apply a random affine map about (0.5,0.5): scale x by s in [0.9,1.1] and y by 1/s (or a small shear up to 0.08), clip into [0.02,0.98], set r0 = 0.9*r, and run SLSQP. Accept if the sum improves. This explores lattice-distortion basins that point moves cannot reach.
backlog.title: Perturbation by rescaling the square (affine stretch) of incumbent

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, read res.v or recompute the multipliers on the active constraints and find the circle with the lowest total contact multiplier (the least constrained, rattler-like). Re-seed by moving that circle to the largest hole and also shrinking its two highest-multiplier neighbours' radii by 10%, then re-solve. Apply to the top 5 pool entries in the post phase instead of random drop-and-replace.
backlog.title: Radius-sum upper-bound-guided restarts via Lagrange multiplier statistics

backlog.spec: Seed with row structures such as 5,5,6,5,5 where row y positions are drawn from a random increasing sequence with gaps in [0.14,0.26] normalized to [0.07,0.93], per-row x jitter offsets uniform in [0,0.5/m], and per-circle noise 0.01. Radii are initialized to 0.5 of the local nearest-neighbour distance. Use for every third start in place of the fixed uniform row spacing.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice with one-row compression using non-uniform row heights

backlog.spec: For 25% of starts, solve the SLSQP problem with the container [0,L]^2 with L=1.06 (walls at 0 and L), then rescale centers and radii by 1/L, treat as a start for the unit-square SLSQP, and re-solve. The slack in the first phase lets circles settle into looser, different topologies before compression.
backlog.title: Anneal the square size: optimize in a larger container then shrink

backlog.spec: Make the container size L a variable fixed per stage. Seed from a random start and solve SLSQP with walls at [0,L] with L=1.15, then re-solve with L=1.08, 1.03 and 1.0, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution scaled by 1/L. Apply this to 30% of random multistarts (it%10 in 0,4,8). The stages are short (maxiter 100), and the last stage is the standard full SLSQP. This differs from the earlier radius-cap and compression seeds because the geometry itself changes. Keep the final validity check.
backlog.title: Container-shrink annealing

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing and re-solve SLSQP once to read the constraint multipliers. SLSQP in scipy does not return them, so recompute them by solving a non-negative least squares on the KKT stationarity condition over the active constraints. Circles whose contacts carry the smallest multipliers are the least useful. Remove the 2 circles with the smallest total multiplier mass, reinsert them at the largest-clearance holes found by sampling, and re-solve. Loop until the time budget ends, and accept only improvements.
backlog.title: Lagrange-multiplier guided relocation

backlog.spec: In the post phase, perturb the incumbent by stretching x by a random factor in [0.9,1.1] and y by the inverse factor, then re-centering into the unit square. Scale the radii by 0.9 and add 0.003 noise, then run SLSQP maxiter 300. Accept the result if the sum of radii improves. Mix this 50/50 with the existing drop-and-replace move.
backlog.title: Affine stretch perturbation

backlog.spec: Seed 25% of the multistarts from a square lattice rotated by a random angle in [0,45 degrees] with random spacing in 0.17 to 0.21. Keep the lattice points that fall inside [0.04,0.96]^2. Trim or pad to 26 points: remove the points closest to the border, or add the points with the largest clearance. Use radii of 0.06 plus noise, then run SLSQP.
backlog.title: Rotated square lattice seeds

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of 6 distinct local optima, treating two optima as the same if their sorted radii differ by less than 1e-3 in L2 norm. In the post phase, pick a pool member at random, perturb it (move 3 random circles, noise 0.02 on the others), and run SLSQP. Replace the worst pool member if the new optimum is better and distinct. Also accept a worse candidate with Metropolis probability, using a temperature of 0.002 that decays to 0.
backlog.title: Basin-dedupe pool with annealed acceptance

backlog.spec: Spend 20% of the budget on multistart SLSQP for n=24 (parametrise n in solve_packing). Take the top 5 solutions. For each, add 2 circles at the two largest holes and shrink all radii by 5%. Run SLSQP with noise at several jitters (10 tries per solution). Feed the best results into the existing post phase. This differs from the 27-to-26 deletion because it grows the circle count.
backlog.title: Variable-n ladder 24 to 26

backlog.spec: Run a pre-stage of SLSQP on 40% of the starts with the added constraints r_i >= 0.03 and r_i <= 0.14, and with a lower bound that tightens from 0.04 to 0 across three stages. This prevents tiny circles early and forces the radii to be balanced. After the last stage, drop the bounds and run the full SLSQP.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius lower-bound regularizer

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in rounds of 150 starts that each get maxiter 25. After each round, keep the top 20% by current sum of radii (projected to feasibility with the finalize shrink). Continue those survivors for 75 more iterations, then keep the top 3 and finish them with a full-precision run. Repeat until 70% of the budget is used. This is successive halving with a different survivor rule from the earlier screen-then-polish attempts. Use the hold-out best seed 0.
backlog.title: Lockstep batched early-culling multistart

backlog.spec: For 20% of the budget, replace SLSQP in the starts with a loop of 60 iterations. In each iteration, solve the LP for radii at fixed centers (scipy linprog, highs). Then move each center along the sum of the dual-weighted contact normals, with a step of 0.2 times the minimum gap. Then run a final SLSQP polish on the 5 best results. The LP duals give directions that the SLSQP basin does not use.
backlog.title: Alternating radius LP and center gradient push

backlog.spec: Build seeds from one hex-packed patch of equal circles of radius 0.09 grown from a random corner. Fill about 12 positions in the patch, then fill the remaining 14 positions with random points that have clearance, using smaller radii of 0.05. Jitter by 0.01 and run SLSQP. Apply to 25% of the starts. This is a mixed-structure seed with an ordered region next to a disordered region.
backlog.title: Two-corner anchored hex patch seeds

incumbent.description: Run multistart for 70% of the time, then repeatedly drop one of the 4 smallest circles from the best packing, re-insert it in the largest sampled hole, and re-optimize all 26 with SLSQP.

memo:
Helped: replacing the hand-built rings with multistart SLSQP using analytic gradients and Jacobians (slot 0, -2.6298). Staggered row seeds added a little (slot 1, -2.6310). Fixed seed 0 with a longer budget gave the biggest later gain (slot 2, -2.6359). The incumbent is slot 8 (-2.6360): multistart for 70% of the time, then drop and re-place small circles. That beats the best known 2.635.

Did not help: other local solvers (slots 3, 9). Seed and start engineering (slots 28, 37, 49, 57). Differential evolution and annealing (-2.6319). n=27 deletion (-2.6319). Constraint pruning (slot 12, broken packing). Symmetry, warm-start, penalty, perturbation, polish, screening and crossover variants all tied at -2.6360 or were worse.

Next: the search looks saturated, and gains are likely 0.0001 at most. Keep the slot 8 structure. Avoid duplicate ideas, since no-edit aborts waste slots. Try a genuinely different basin structure, or stop.
